subproblem.title: A stationary varifold whose planes contain the position vector has n-homogeneous weight (corrected 5.3, step A5)
subproblem.statement: Let C be an n-varifold on ℝ^N (C : Varifold N n univ) which is stationary in ℝ^N and satisfies p_S(y) = y (i.e. y ∈ S) for C-a.e. (y,S), where p_S = Grassmannian.project S is the orthogonal projection onto S. Then μ_C(s·A) = s^n μ_C(A) for every s > 0 and every set A ⊆ ℝ^N (in ℝ≥0∞: C.weight (s • A) = ofReal s ^ n * C.weight A). This is the corrected form of Simon 5.3.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (C : Varifold N n (univ : Set (Euclidean N))), C.Stationary → (∀ᵐ z ∂C.measure, Grassmannian.project z.2 z.1 = z.1) → ∀ (s : ℝ) (A : Set (Euclidean N)), 0 < s → C.weight (s • A) = ENNReal.ofReal s ^ n * C.weight A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step A5 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 8, p. 215: '5.3 by the same argument as in the proof of Theorem 6.1 of Ch. 4, except that we use 3.5'; the cited Ch. 4 Theorem 6.1 is not present in this edition, so the argument is written out; it is 3.5 with V = C, x = 0, φ(r/ρ) ≡ 1 on spt h, where the defect term vanishes because y ∈ S a.e. and δC = 0). ERRATUM: printed 5.3 'λ^{-n}μ_C(η_{0,λ}(A)) = μ_C(A)' has the wrong power; the correct statement is μ_C(sA) = s^nμ_C(A) (SimonGMT TangentScalingCounterexample). Notation: μ := C.weight = (C.measure).map Prod.fst, a Borel measure on ℝ^N that is finite on compact sets (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact with U = ℝ^N); p_S := Grassmannian.project S; Dg(y) is the derivative of g at y.
1. (Identity (H).) Let g : ℝ^N → ℝ be C¹ with compact support. X(y) := g(y)•y is C¹, and support X ⊆ support g, so X has compact support and tsupport X ⊆ ℝ^N; thus X ∈ Varifold.TestVectorField univ, and stationarity gives C.firstVariation X = 0. By SimonGMT Varifold.tangentialDivergence_smul (RadialFirstVariation.lean:257) with h = g and the identity field, div_S X(y) = g(y)·div_S(id)(y) + Dg(y)(p_S y), and div_S(id)(y) = trace(S·Id) = trace S = n (the Jacobian matrix of the identity is the identity matrix; Grassmannian.trace_eq). So div_S X(y) = n·g(y) + Dg(y)(p_S y), and by hypothesis this equals n·g(y) + Dg(y)(y) for C-a.e. (y,S). The function y ↦ n·g(y) + Dg(y)(y) is continuous with compact support, and integrating a function of y alone against C.measure is integrating it against μ (integral_map along the measurable map Prod.fst). Hence
 (H) ∫ (n·g(y) + Dg(y)(y)) dμ(y) = 0 for every g ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N).
2. (Scaling identity for C¹_c functions.) Fix g ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N), choose R_g > 0 with tsupport g ⊆ B_{R_g}(0), and let L := sup_y ‖Dg(y)‖ < ∞ (Dg is continuous with compact support). For s > 0 put F(s) := ∫ g(s^{-1}y) dμ(y); the integrand is continuous and vanishes outside the compact set B_{sR_g}(0), so it is integrable.
 (a) F is differentiable at every s0 > 0 with F'(s0) = −s0^{-1}∫ Dg(s0^{-1}y)(s0^{-1}y) dμ(y). Indeed, for each y the map s ↦ g(s^{-1}y) has derivative Dg(s^{-1}y)(−s^{-2}y) = −s^{-1}·Dg(s^{-1}y)(s^{-1}y) at every s > 0. For s ∈ (s0/2, 2s0) this derivative vanishes unless ‖s^{-1}y‖ ≤ R_g, in which case ‖y‖ ≤ 2s0R_g and its absolute value is ≤ s^{-1}·L·R_g ≤ 2LR_g/s0. So all these derivatives are dominated by b(y) := (2LR_g/s0)·1_{B_{2s0R_g}(0)}(y), which is μ-integrable because μ(B_{2s0R_g}(0)) < ∞; the integrands are continuous (hence measurable) and F(s0) is finite. Differentiation under the integral sign (Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le on the neighbourhood (s0/2, 2s0) of s0) gives the claim.
 (b) For s > 0 let g_s(y) := g(s^{-1}y). Then g_s ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N) and, by the chain rule, Dg_s(y)(v) = Dg(s^{-1}y)(s^{-1}v), so Dg_s(y)(y) = Dg(s^{-1}y)(s^{-1}y). Applying (H) to g_s and splitting the integral (both summands are continuous with compact support, hence integrable): n·F(s) + ∫ Dg(s^{-1}y)(s^{-1}y) dμ(y) = 0.
 (c) By (a) and (b), F'(s) = n·F(s)/s for all s > 0. Let G(s) := s^{-n}F(s) for s > 0. Then G'(s) = −n·s^{-n-1}F(s) + s^{-n}F'(s) = 0 for every s > 0, so G is constant on the interval (0,∞) (a function with zero derivative on an open interval is constant, e.g. is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero / IsOpen.is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero on the convex set (0,∞)). Hence F(s) = s^nG(s) = s^nG(1) = s^nF(1), i.e.
 (S) ∫ g(s^{-1}y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ for all s > 0 and all g ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N).
3. (Extension of (S) to C_c.) Let g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and s > 0. For k ∈ ℕ let φ_k be the normalized smooth bump function of Mathlib ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^N) with rOut = 1/(k+1) (normed with respect to Lebesgue measure): φ_k ≥ 0, ∫ φ_k = 1, support φ_k = B°_{1/(k+1)}(0). Put g_k := φ_k ⋆ g. Then g_k is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left: φ_k is smooth with compact support and g is locally integrable); support g_k ⊆ K₁ := tsupport g + B_1(0), a compact set independent of k, so g_k ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N); and |g_k(y) − g(y)| ≤ ε_k := sup{|g(y') − g(y'')| : ‖y' − y''‖ ≤ 1/(k+1)} for every y (ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le), where ε_k → 0 by uniform continuity of the compactly supported continuous g. By (S), ∫ g_k(s^{-1}y) dμ(y) = s^n∫ g_k dμ for every k. Moreover |∫ g_k(s^{-1}y)dμ − ∫ g(s^{-1}y)dμ| ≤ ε_k·μ(s•K₁) and |∫ g_k dμ − ∫ g dμ| ≤ ε_k·μ(K₁), because the differences vanish outside the compact sets s•K₁ and K₁ respectively, and μ is finite on compact sets. Letting k → ∞ gives ∫ g(s^{-1}y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and s > 0.
4. (Equality of measures.) Fix s > 0 and let T(y) := s^{-1}•y, a linear homeomorphism of ℝ^N and hence a measurable equivalence. Put ν₁ := μ.map T and ν₂ := ofReal(s)^n • μ. Both are locally finite: for compact K, ν₁(K) = μ(T^{-1}K) = μ(s•K) < ∞ (s•K is compact) and ν₂(K) = ofReal(s)^n·μ(K) < ∞. On ℝ^N, a locally compact second-countable metric space, locally finite Borel measures are regular (Mathlib instance Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). For g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N): ∫ g dν₁ = ∫ g(s^{-1}y) dμ(y) (integral_map) = s^n∫ g dμ (step 3) = (ofReal(s)^n).toReal·∫ g dμ = ∫ g dν₂ (integral_smul_measure). By uniqueness in the Riesz representation theorem (Mathlib Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported) ν₁ = ν₂.
5. (All sets.) Let A ⊆ ℝ^N be arbitrary (not necessarily measurable). Since T is a measurable equivalence, (μ.map T)(A) = μ(T^{-1}(A)) for every set A (MeasurableEquiv.map_apply), and T^{-1}(A) = {y : s^{-1}•y ∈ A} = s•A (y = s•(s^{-1}•y)). Hence μ(s•A) = ν₁(A) = ν₂(A) = ofReal(s)^n·μ(A), i.e. C.weight (s • A) = ENNReal.ofReal s ^ n * C.weight A.
proof_key_steps: Stationarity with X = g(y)y and tangentialDivergence_smul (div_S id = trace S = n), plus p_S(y) = y a.e.: ∫(n g + Dg(y)y) dμ_C = 0 for all g ∈ C¹_c.
F(s) = ∫ g(y/s) dμ_C is differentiable (dominated differentiation) with F'(s) = −s⁻¹∫Dg(y/s)(y/s)dμ_C = nF(s)/s by the identity applied to g(·/s); so s^{-n}F(s) is constant.
Mollification extends ∫ g(y/s) dμ_C = s^n∫ g dμ_C from C¹_c to C_c.
Riesz uniqueness: (y ↦ y/s)_#μ_C = s^nμ_C as regular measures; MeasurableEquiv.map_apply gives μ_C(s•A) = s^nμ_C(A) for every set A.

audit.reason: Stationarity and radial projection equality yield identity H without assuming homogeneity. The supplied domination justifies differentiation; the resulting ODE gives scaling for C¹ compactly supported functions. Mollification with a common compact support, Riesz uniqueness, and measurable-equivalence map evaluation extend this to every set A. The proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Rescaled ball masses converge to θ ω_n R^n (fact R1 of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^N, let V be an n-varifold on U (V : Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, θ ∈ [0,∞] and R > 0. Suppose Θ^n(μ_V, x) exists and equals θ, i.e. HasDensity n μ_V x θ (lim_{ρ↓0} μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) = θ with closed balls). Then, with V_{x,t} := rescaledMeasure V x t = t^{-n}·(η_{x,t})_#V, η_{x,t}(z,S) = (t^{-1}(z−x), S), V_{x,t}(B_R(0) × G(N,n)) → θ·ω_n·R^n as t ↓ 0 (in ℝ≥0∞: θ * unitBallVolume n * ofReal R ^ n). No hypothesis x ∈ U, θ < ∞ or bounded first variation is needed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (θ : ℝ≥0∞) (R : ℝ), HasDensity n V.weight x θ → 0 < R → Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ rescaledMeasure V x t (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) R ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ * unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal R ^ n))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: fact R1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 8, p. 215, the mass computation behind 5.1–5.2; SimonGMT Varifold.blowUpWeight_closedBall, TangentRescaling.lean:119, rescaledMeasure V x t being V.blowUpMeasure x t after unfolding Chapter03.blowUpMap). Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n = volume(B°_1(0) ⊆ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)); G := Grassmannian N n; μ_V := V.weight = (V.measure).map Prod.fst; K_R := closedBall 0 R ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ^N × G.
1. (Constants.) The open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is nonempty, open and bounded, and volume on this finite-dimensional space is an additive Haar measure; hence 0 < ω < ∞ (Mathlib Metric.measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top; for n = 0 the space is a point and ω = 1). For t > 0 the numbers a := ofReal t and r := ofReal R lie in (0,∞), hence so do a^n, r^n and ω·r^n.
2. (Exact formula for t > 0.) Fix t > 0 and let φ_t(z,S) := (t^{-1}•(z − x), S); φ_t is continuous, hence measurable. K_R is closed, hence measurable, so by the definition rescaledMeasure V x t = ofReal((t^{-1})^n) • V.measure.map φ_t together with Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply, rescaledMeasure V x t (K_R) = ofReal((t^{-1})^n) · V.measure(φ_t^{-1}(K_R)). Since ‖t^{-1}•(z − x)‖ = t^{-1}‖z − x‖, we have ‖t^{-1}•(z − x)‖ ≤ R ⟺ ‖z − x‖ ≤ tR, so φ_t^{-1}(K_R) = closedBall x (tR) ×ˢ univ. By Varifold.weight_apply (closed balls are measurable), V.measure(closedBall x (tR) ×ˢ univ) = μ_V(closedBall x (tR)). Hence rescaledMeasure V x t (K_R) = ofReal((t^{-1})^n) · μ_V(B_{tR}(x)).
3. (Rewriting through the density ratio.) For t > 0, ofReal((t^{-1})^n) = (a^n)^{-1} (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos and ENNReal.ofReal_pow), and ofReal(tR)^n = a^n·r^n (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, mul_pow). By definition densityRatio n μ_V x (tR) = μ_V(B_{tR}(x)) / (ω·ofReal(tR)^n), so densityRatio n μ_V x (tR) · (ω·r^n) = μ_V(B_{tR}(x)) · (ω·a^n·r^n)^{-1} · ω · r^n = μ_V(B_{tR}(x)) · (a^n)^{-1}, because (ω·a^n·r^n)^{-1} = ω^{-1}(a^n)^{-1}(r^n)^{-1} (ENNReal.mul_inv; all factors are nonzero and finite) and ω^{-1}ω = (r^n)^{-1}r^n = 1. Together with step 2: for every t > 0, rescaledMeasure V x t (K_R) = densityRatio n μ_V x (tR) · (ω·r^n).
4. (Limit.) The map t ↦ tR is continuous, sends 0 to 0 and (0,∞) into (0,∞), so Tendsto (fun t ↦ t·R) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝[>] 0). Composing with the hypothesis HasDensity n μ_V x θ, i.e. Tendsto (densityRatio n μ_V x) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 θ), gives densityRatio n μ_V x (tR) → θ as t ↓ 0. Multiplying by the constant ω·r^n, which is ≠ ∞ (so the side condition of ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const holds), gives densityRatio n μ_V x (tR)·(ω·r^n) → θ·(ω·r^n) = θ·ω·r^n.
5. (Conclusion.) The identity of step 3 holds for all t ∈ (0,∞), a set belonging to 𝓝[>] 0, so the two functions agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0 (Filter.Tendsto.congr'). Hence rescaledMeasure V x t (closedBall 0 R ×ˢ univ) → θ · unitBallVolume n · ofReal R ^ n as t ↓ 0. (If θ = ∞ the limit is ∞, consistently, since ω·r^n ≠ 0.)

subproblem.title: First-variation scaling bound for the rescalings V_{x,t} (fact R2 of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on the open set U ⊆ ℝ^N with locally bounded first variation, x ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0, R > 0 with closed ball B_{tR}(x) ⊆ U, M ∈ ℝ, and X : ℝ^N → ℝ^N a C¹ vector field with compact support, tsupport X ⊆ B°_R(0) (open ball) and |X(y)| ≤ M for all y. Then |∫ div_S X(y) dV_{x,t}(y,S)| ≤ M · R^{n−1} · (tR)^{1−n}‖δV‖(B_{tR}(x)), where V_{x,t} = rescaledMeasure V x t, div_S X = Varifold.tangentialDivergence X and ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V; in ℝ≥0∞: ofReal|∫ div_S X dV_{x,t}| ≤ ofReal M · (ofReal R^n / ofReal R) · (ofReal(tR)·‖δV‖(B_{tR}(x)) / ofReal(tR)^n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (t R M : ℝ) (X : Euclidean N → Euclidean N), V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation → 0 < t → 0 < R → closedBall x (t * R) ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ ball (0 : Euclidean N) R → (∀ y, ‖X y‖ ≤ M) → ENNReal.ofReal |∫ z, Varifold.tangentialDivergence X z.1 z.2 ∂(rescaledMeasure V x t)| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal M * (ENNReal.ofReal R ^ n / ENNReal.ofReal R) * (ENNReal.ofReal (t * R) * variationMeasure V (closedBall x (t * R)) / ENNReal.ofReal (t * R) ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: fact R2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 8: 'by definition of δV (in 2)', p. 215; the bound |δV(Y)| ≤ sup|Y|·‖δV‖(W) for spt Y ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U is the defining property 2.5 of ‖δV‖ — the parent derives the same inequality from 2.6). Notation: G := Grassmannian N n; div_S X(w) := Varifold.tangentialDivergence X w S = trace(S·DX(w)); ‖δV‖ := variationMeasure V; δV(Y) := V.firstVariation Y = ∫ div_S Y(z) dV(z,S).
1. (Set-up.) ψ(z) := t^{-1}•(z − x) is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^N with inverse w ↦ x + t•w, and φ(z,S) := (ψ z, S) is continuous. f(w,S) := div_S X(w) is continuous (SimonGMT Varifold.continuous_tangentialDivergence, X ∈ C¹) with compact support (Varifold.hasCompactSupport_tangentialDivergence), hence bounded and Borel. Also M ≥ 0, because 0 ≤ ‖X 0‖ ≤ M.
2. (Change of variables.) By definition rescaledMeasure V x t = ofReal((t^{-1})^n) • V.measure.map φ. By integral_smul_measure (the real number (ofReal((t^{-1})^n)).toReal equals (t^{-1})^n ≥ 0) and integral_map (φ measurable, f continuous): ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) = (t^{-1})^n · ∫ f(φ(z,S)) dV.measure(z,S).
3. (The pulled-back field.) Put Y(z) := t • X(ψ z). Y is C¹ (C¹ map composed with an affine map, times a constant). By the chain rule DY(z) = t·DX(ψ z)∘(t^{-1}·Id) = DX(ψ z); hence the Jacobian matrix of Y at z equals that of X at ψ z and div_S Y(z) = trace(S·DY(z)) = div_S X(ψ z) = f(φ(z,S)) for all (z,S). Therefore ∫ f∘φ dV.measure = ∫ div_S Y(z) dV(z,S) = δV(Y), and by step 2, ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) = (t^{-1})^n·δV(Y).
4. (Support and size of Y.) Y(z) ≠ 0 iff X(ψ z) ≠ 0, so support Y = ψ^{-1}(support X), and since ψ is a homeomorphism, tsupport Y = ψ^{-1}(tsupport X). Thus tsupport Y is compact, and tsupport Y ⊆ ψ^{-1}(B°_R(0)) = B°_{tR}(x) (because ‖ψ z‖ < R ⟺ ‖z − x‖ < tR) ⊆ B_{tR}(x) ⊆ U. Hence Y (with these properties) is an element of Varifold.TestVectorField U. Moreover ‖Y z‖ = t‖X(ψ z)‖ ≤ tM for every z.
5. (Bound by the supremum in 2.5.) Let W := B°_{tR}(x). W is open, closure W ⊆ B_{tR}(x) ⊆ U, and closure W is compact (a closed subset of a compact closed ball). If M = 0, then X ≡ 0, so Y ≡ 0, div_S Y ≡ 0 (Varifold.tangentialDivergence_zero), δV(Y) = 0, the left side of the claim is 0 and there is nothing to prove. Let M > 0, c := (tM)^{-1} > 0 and Ŷ := c•Y. Then Ŷ is C¹ with compact support, tsupport Ŷ = tsupport Y ⊆ W ⊆ U and ‖Ŷ z‖ ≤ 1 for all z, i.e. Ŷ ∈ TestVectorField U with Ŷ.UnitSupportedIn W. By the definition of Varifold.firstVariationNormOn as the supremum, over such test fields, of ofReal|δV(·)|, we get ofReal|δV(Ŷ)| ≤ V.firstVariationNormOn W. By linearity (Varifold.firstVariation_const_smul) δV(Ŷ) = c·δV(Y), so ofReal|δV(Y)| = ofReal(tM)·ofReal|δV(Ŷ)| ≤ ofReal(tM)·V.firstVariationNormOn W.
6. (Identification with ‖δV‖.) Since V has locally bounded first variation, variationMeasure V = V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV (definition of variationMeasure, dif_pos), and by Simon 2.5 in the kernel-checked form SimonGMT Varifold.firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm (FirstVariationRiesz.lean:218; W open with compact closure contained in U) V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV W = V.firstVariationNormOn W. As W ⊆ B_{tR}(x), monotonicity gives V.firstVariationNormOn W = ‖δV‖(W) ≤ ‖δV‖(B_{tR}(x)) =: A.
7. (Assembly.) By steps 3, 5, 6: ofReal|∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t)| = ofReal((t^{-1})^n)·ofReal|δV(Y)| ≤ ofReal((t^{-1})^n)·ofReal t·ofReal M·A. With a := ofReal t and r := ofReal R, both in (0,∞): ofReal((t^{-1})^n) = (a^n)^{-1}, ofReal(tR) = a·r and ofReal(tR)^n = a^n·r^n. In ℝ≥0∞, ofReal M·(r^n/r)·(a·r·A/(a^n·r^n)) = ofReal M·a·A·(a^n)^{-1}·(r^n·(r^n)^{-1})·(r^{-1}·r) = ofReal M·a·A·(a^n)^{-1}, using (a^n·r^n)^{-1} = (a^n)^{-1}(r^n)^{-1} (ENNReal.mul_inv, both factors nonzero and finite) and r^n(r^n)^{-1} = r^{-1}r = 1; this holds also when A = ∞. The right-hand side is exactly the bound obtained, which proves the claim.
proof_key_steps: Change of variables: ∫ div_S X dV_{x,t} = (t⁻¹)^n ∫ div_S X(t⁻¹(z−x)) dV(z,S).
Y(z) := t·X(t⁻¹(z−x)) has DY(z) = DX(t⁻¹(z−x)), so the integral is (t⁻¹)^n·δV(Y); Y ∈ K(U;ℝ^N), tsupport Y ⊆ B°_{tR}(x), |Y| ≤ tM.
Scale Y to a unit test field supported in W = B°_{tR}(x): |δV(Y)| ≤ tM·firstVariationNormOn V W (definition 2.5).
SimonGMT firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm: firstVariationNormOn V W = ‖δV‖(W) ≤ ‖δV‖(B_{tR}(x)).
ENNReal arithmetic: (t⁻¹)^n·t·M·A = M·(R^n/R)·(tR·A/(tR)^n).

subproblem.title: Restricting a vaguely convergent sequence to an open set gives Radon convergence of varifolds on that set
subproblem.statement: Let Ω ⊆ ℝ^N, c ∈ [0,∞), and let μ_i (i ∈ ℕ), μ be Borel measures on ℝ^N × G(N,n) with μ_i → μ vaguely, i.e. ∫ f dμ_i → ∫ f dμ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n)) (VagueConverges). Let W_i (i ∈ ℕ) and W be n-varifolds on Ω (Varifold N n Ω) whose measures are W_i.measure = c·(μ_i ⌞ (Ω × G)) and W.measure = c·(μ ⌞ (Ω × G)). Then W_i → W as Radon measures on G_n(Ω), i.e. Varifold.RadonConverges W_· W (convergence of ∫ f d(W_i)_dom for every f ∈ C_c(Ω × G)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Euclidean N)) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (Ws : ℕ → Varifold N n Ω) (W : Varifold N n Ω) (c : ℝ≥0∞), VagueConverges μs μ → c ≠ ∞ → (∀ i, (Ws i).measure = c • (μs i).restrict (Ω ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))) → W.measure = c • μ.restrict (Ω ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) → Varifold.RadonConverges Ws W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step B2 of the parent proof ('every f ∈ C_c(Ω × G) (subtype) extends by zero to f̃ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport ⊆ Ω × G, and ∫ f d(W_j)_dom = ∫ f̃ dV_{x,t_j} → ∫ f̃ dC = ∫ f d(C_Ω)_dom'), stated for general measures and a general constant. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n (compact Hausdorff); P := Ω ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ^N × G; val : P → ℝ^N × G the inclusion of the subspace; for a varifold Z on Ω, Z.domainMeasure = Z.measure.comap val (SimonGMT Varifold.lean). Varifold.RadonConverges Ws W means: for every f ∈ C_c(P, ℝ), ∫ f d(Ws i).domainMeasure → ∫ f dW.domainMeasure.
1. (P is open.) Ω is open because W is a varifold on Ω (field W.isOpen_domain), so P = Ω ×ˢ univ is open, in particular measurable, and val is an open embedding and a measurable embedding (MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe).
2. (Zero extension.) Fix f ∈ C_c(P, ℝ). Define f̃ : ℝ^N × G → ℝ by f̃(z) := f(⟨z, h⟩) if h : z ∈ P, and f̃(z) := 0 if z ∉ P. Then f̃ ∘ val = f and f̃ = 0 off P. Let Q := val(tsupport f); it is compact (continuous image of the compact set tsupport f), hence closed in the Hausdorff space ℝ^N × G, and Q ⊆ P.
 (a) f̃ is continuous at every z ∈ P: P is an open neighbourhood of z and, val being an open embedding, continuity of f̃ at z is equivalent to continuity of f̃ ∘ val = f at ⟨z, h⟩ (IsOpenEmbedding.continuousAt_iff), which holds.
 (b) f̃ is continuous at every z ∉ P: then z ∉ Q, and on the open neighbourhood Qᶜ of z we have f̃ ≡ 0 (for w ∈ Qᶜ: if w ∉ P then f̃ w = 0 by definition; if w ∈ P then ⟨w,_⟩ ∉ tsupport f, so f(⟨w,_⟩) = 0). A function that is locally constant near z is continuous at z.
 (c) support f̃ ⊆ Q, so tsupport f̃ ⊆ Q (Q closed) is compact. Hence f̃ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).
3. (Integrals against varifolds on Ω.) For any varifold Z on Ω, ∫ f dZ.domainMeasure = ∫ f̃ dZ.measure: indeed Z.domainMeasure.map val = Z.measure (SimonGMT Varifold.map_domainMeasure) and, val being a measurable embedding, ∫ f̃ d(Z.domainMeasure.map val) = ∫ f̃ ∘ val dZ.domainMeasure = ∫ f dZ.domainMeasure (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
4. (Integrals against the restricted measures.) For any measure ν on ℝ^N × G, ∫ f̃ d(c • ν.restrict P) = c.toReal · ∫_P f̃ dν = c.toReal · ∫ f̃ dν, by integral_smul_measure and, since f̃ = 0 off P, setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (neither identity needs integrability).
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3, 4 and the hypotheses on the measures of Ws i and W, ∫ f d(Ws i).domainMeasure = c.toReal · ∫ f̃ dμ_i for every i, and ∫ f dW.domainMeasure = c.toReal · ∫ f̃ dμ. By VagueConverges μs μ applied to f̃ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ), ∫ f̃ dμ_i → ∫ f̃ dμ; multiplying by the constant c.toReal (Tendsto.const_mul) gives ∫ f d(Ws i).domainMeasure → ∫ f dW.domainMeasure. Since f ∈ C_c(P, ℝ) was arbitrary, Varifold.RadonConverges Ws W. (The hypothesis c ≠ ∞ is not needed by this argument; it is part of the intended use c = τ^{-1}.)
proof_key_steps: P = Ω ×ˢ univ is open (W.isOpen_domain); val : P → ℝ^N×G is an open measurable embedding.
Extend f ∈ C_c(P) by zero: f̃ is continuous (open embedding on P; vanishes on the open complement of the compact closed set val(tsupport f)) with compact support.
∫ f d Z.domainMeasure = ∫ f̃ dZ.measure (map_domainMeasure + MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map) and ∫ f̃ d(c•ν⌞P) = c.toReal∫ f̃ dν.
Vague convergence on f̃ gives Radon convergence on Ω.

Recall C.weight(closedBall 0 r) = C.measure(K_r) (Varifold.weight_apply) and C.measure(K_r) < ∞ (C.finite_on_compact with the compact set closedBall 0 r ⊆ univ).
1. (Data and mass limits.) By IsVarifoldTangent V x C there are t_j > 0, t_j → 0 with VagueConverges (j ↦ V_j) C.measure, V_j := rescaledMeasure V x t_j. Since t_j > 0 and t_j → 0, Tendsto t atTop (𝓝[>] 0). Composing with the sibling rescaled_ball_mass (applied with θ := ofReal θ0 and radius r) gives m_j(r) := V_j(K_r) → L(r) for every r > 0. In particular, as L(r) < ∞, m_j(r) < ∞ for all large j.
2. (Cut-off functions.) For 0 < a < b let h_{a,b}(y) := min(1, max(0, (b − ‖y‖)/(b − a))) and F_{a,b}(y,S) := h_{a,b}(y). F_{a,b} is continuous, 0 ≤ F_{a,b} ≤ 1, F_{a,b} = 1 on K_a and F_{a,b} = 0 off ball 0 b ×ˢ univ; its support lies in K_b, which is compact (closed ball times the compact G). So F_{a,b} ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ) and 1_{K_a} ≤ F_{a,b} ≤ 1_{K_b} pointwise.
3. (Integral comparison.)
